+# Incident Postmortem: Edge Client Request Jitter & Booklogr API Latency Spike
+
+## Root Cause
+Commit `310d4bb5c6b8698f087da4d0faf69fef0e5c071e` ("Order library list by shelf position") refactored `get_books()` in `api/routes/books.py`. Instead of delegating sorting and pagination to the database via SQL `ORDER BY` and `paginate()`, the route was changed to load all records into application memory (`books.all()`), execute Python-level Unicode decomposition and title normalization (`unicodedata.normalize`) on every record, and slice the results in memory. On large dataset requests, this in-memory processing generated heavy CPU overhead and caused HTTP request latencies to spike up to ~5 seconds, triggering flapping jitter on traffic generators and p99 latency alerts.
+
+## Evidence
+- Alertmanager firing alerts:
+  - `EdgeClientRequestJitter`: Flapping request jitter detected on edge client traffic generator.
+  - `BooklogrApiLatencyP99High`: p99 HTTP request latency reached ~5s for `booklogr-api`.
+- Prometheus metrics (`flask_http_request_duration_seconds`):
+  - Average latency for `GET /v1/books` endpoint spiked to 2.8s - 5s+.
+- Git commit inspection (`git log`, `git show 310d4bb5c6b8698f087da4d0faf69fef0e5c071e`):
+  - Identified recent commit modifying `api/routes/books.py` to replace database pagination with in-memory loading (`books.all()`) and sorting.
+
+## Key Changes Made
+- Reverted commit `310d4bb5c6b8698f087da4d0faf69fef0e5c071e` in `api/routes/books.py`.
+- Restored SQL-level sorting (`books.order_by(...)`) and pagination (`books.paginate(...)`) for `GET /v1/books`, eliminating the in-memory sorting bottleneck.
